solutions.latex: The points trend downward with moderate scatter: a moderate negative correlation. Answer A.
$f'(x)=6x^2+2x$, $f''(x)=12x+2$. Concave down when $f''(x)<0$: $12x+2<0$, so $x<-\dfrac{1}{6}$. Answer A.
Amplitude $=1$. Period $=\dfrac{2\pi}{n}$ with $n=\pi$, so period $=\dfrac{2\pi}{\pi}=2$. Answer A.
$y=2-(x+1)^2$ is a downward parabola with vertex $(-1,2)$ and $y$-intercept $1$... the vertex lies to the left of the $y$-axis, at height $2$. Answer D.
Adding a constant shifts the mean by 4 but leaves the spread unchanged. Answer B.
$\sin x=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, related angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, sine negative in the 3rd and 4th quadrants: $x=\pi+\dfrac{\pi}{3},\ 2\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{4\pi}{3},\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$. Answer C.
4 quarters per year at $16\%\div4=4\%$ per quarter. Table value (4 periods, 4%) $=4.25$. $28475=4.25\times x$, so $x=\dfrac{28475}{4.25}=6700$. Answer C.
$(n-80)(n-40)=0$, so $n=40$ or $n=80$. When $n=40$, $T_{40}=-2(40)+121=\$41$ (sensible). When $n=80$, $T_{80}=-2(80)+121=-\$39$, a negative repayment, so $n=80$ is not a sensible solution.
Right triangle with opposite $2$, adjacent $3$, hypotenuse $\sqrt{13}$. $\sin\theta=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{13}}$
$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=3x^2+2$ (the scanned working writes $3x^2+2x$, an error; see notes).
At $P$: $m_1=2^3+2(2)-7=5$, so the normal has gradient $-\dfrac15$. $y-4=-\dfrac15(x-2)$, $5y-20=-x+2$, so $x+5y-22=0$.
$x^2=30^2+22^2-2(30)(22)\cos60^\circ=724$, $x=\sqrt{724}\approx26.907$. The distance between $B$ and $C$ is $27$ km.
Upper half: $A\approx\dfrac{420-0}{2\times6}\{30+2(40+60+80+60+40)+30\}=35\times620=21700$. Total area of the lake $\approx 2\times21700=43400\ \text{m}^2$.
$v=-6\sin2t$. At rest when $v=0$: $\sin2t=0$, $t=0,\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pi$. The particle first comes to rest after $t=0$ at $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, where $x=1+3\cos\pi=-2$: 2 m to the left of the origin.

$a=-12\cos2t$. Greatest magnitude of velocity when $a=0$: $\cos2t=0$, $2t=\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\ldots$, so $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4},\dfrac{3\pi}{4},\ldots$. At $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $v=-6\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}=-6$; the maximum speed is $6$ m/s.

$2(1-\cos^2x)+\cos x-2=0\Rightarrow-2\cos^2x+\cos x=0\Rightarrow\cos x(1-2\cos x)=0$. $\cos x=0$: $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$. $\cos x=\dfrac12$: $x=\dfrac{\pi}{3},\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$. So $x=\dfrac{\pi}{3},\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$.
Strong positive association. (c) involves interpolation (very reliable); (d) involves extrapolation (less reliable).
High tide when $h=4$: $t=4$ or $t=20$ (4 a.m. and 8 p.m.).
$h(10)=4\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\times10\right)=4\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{4}\approx-2.8$. The tide is 2.8 m below mean height.
